chunks: About a man who prays four rak'ahs while traveling out of forgetfulness, he said: “If he remembers on that day, then he should repeat it; and if he does not remember until that day passes, then there is no repetition upon him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ: four, referring to the full number of rak'ahs prayed mistakenly
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which the prayer is shortened
key_terms.فَلَا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no obligation of repetition upon him
key_terms.فَلْيُعِدْ: then he should repeat the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do if he prays four rak'ahs by mistake instead of the shortened prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the traveler who performs a four-rak'ah prayer instead of the shortened prayer out of forgetfulness. If he remembers within the same day, he must repeat the prayer; if the day has passed before he remembers, no repeat is required.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1274 - Abu Basir asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about a man who, while traveling, prays four rak'ahs (instead of two) out of forgetfulness.
The Imam said: "If he remembers it on that same day, he should repeat (the prayer). If he does not remember until the day has passed, then there is no need for him to repeat it”.
